hook: 5 Steps To Support Good Nails and Hair
claim: Keragenis is a capsule sold for healthy nails and hair, including toenail problems. The sales letter is written by 'Benjamin Jones', who says he has researched nail and hair health for 17 years.
story: The letter uses the same template we've seen on several other products: a $69 one-time price, an 'FDA approved and GMP certified facility', and a warning that restocking 'rare ingredients' takes months.
ing_note: The letter names these ingredients 'such as'; the full label and amounts aren't shown.
price_note: 3- and 6-bottle packages are discounted, with free shipping on every order; totals appear on the order page.
refund_note: The seller promises a full refund within 60 days even if the bottle is used up.
checks: None of the named ingredients has evidence for nail fungus, brittle nails or hair growth.
Biotin, the most common nail supplement, helps only in deficiency and isn't named.
Nail fungus needs an antifungal treatment; hair loss has several causes (thyroid, iron, hormones) that a doctor can test for.
cons: Ingredients don't match nail or hair goals
verdict: Keragenis uses general antioxidant herbs that have nothing specific to do with nails or hair. For brittle nails, fungal nails or thinning hair, a doctor or dermatologist can find the cause and offer treatments that work.
